name: Manage Skills (self-improvement engine)
summary: Create, update, delete your own skills. This is your primary self-improvement mechanism. Called automatically before unknown tasks AND after every task where you improvised.

steps.note: Always check what exists first. Note version numbers. Version 1 = untested draft, 2+ = battle-tested.
Read the specific skill before updating it. Check what's already there.

steps.action: write_skill(skill_id, name, summary, triggers, steps, notes)
steps.note: Version auto-increments on update. Use same skill_id to update, new id to create. Steps MUST reference actual tool names. Notes MUST have at least one gotcha.
delete_skill(skill_id). Only when superseded by a better skill or the approach is fundamentally broken.
Track that you improved. This metric shows you are getting better.

notes: SKILL-FIRST RULE: call write_skill BEFORE executing an unknown task type, not after.
AFTER-TASK RULE: mandatory write_skill after any improvisation, even small ones.
Good skill anatomy: triggers (specific, 3-8 entries), steps (tool calls, not vague actions), notes (gotchas, AVOID patterns).
AVOID: creating duplicate skills — always check list_skills first.
AVOID: vague step descriptions like 'search for it' — write 'web_search(query)' instead.
The notes array is the most valuable part — that's where hard-won lessons live.
Every AVOID note prevents a future mistake. Write them even when it feels obvious.
